findings.defect:
Several readouts leave their windows at values the real mission reaches, and no lab view reaches them.
- Clock row: 'T+ 7d 20:33:51 PHYSICS ×4' puts the ×4 at x ≈375-403 against a panel edge at ≈379 (mission 14, 15, 16, 17). 'T+ 5d 03:23:57 RAILS ×100' runs to x ≈404 (mission 12, 13), and 'RAILS ×50' does the same in mission 08. The warp factor sits outside the panel for the whole mid-mission and entry.
- Speed window: 'SURFACE 10 835.5 m/s | HDG 333°' runs to x ≈1530 against a border at ≈1491 (mission 14). 'ORBIT 10 847.9 m/s | HDG 091°' touches it (07). So the window breaks during TLI and the lunar-return entry, the two most watched moments.
- ORBIT apsis rows: the value runs into its countdown, as in 'APOAPSIS 506.8 MmT− 10d 08:11' (12, 13) and 'PERIAPSIS 185.1 kmT− 11d 19:00' (07).
- RECOVERY rows: 'ENTRY INTERFACE 2 035 km · 318°' / '3 982 km · 345°' run over the panel's right padding and border (04, 12, 13, 14).
findings.realReference: KSP / KSP 2: the MET, the warp indicator and the navball speed readout stay inside their frames at every value (speed up to 5 digits, MET in years and days). The brief asks for AAA quality, and readouts printed over a panel border fail that at a glance.
findings.likelyCause:
src/ui/hud/hudStyles.ts:
- .hud .bottom .speed is a fixed width (calc(var(--u) * 29)) with contain: size, so 5-digit speeds overflow.
- .hud .clock .metrow is flex space-between with contain: size and no shrink or second line for the warp word.
- .hud .orbit .apsis is a grid 'auto 1fr auto' whose gap 2bd0a88 narrowed from 0.8u to 0.5u, so the value column collapses into the countdown at 10-day values.
- The target rows are nowrap.
The lab scenes (labs/flight-ui/main.ts SETUP) never combine a day-count MET with a warp word, a speed of 10 km/s or more, a 10-day countdown, or a long entry-interface row, so expectTextFloor and the no-overflow checks never see these strings.
findings.fixDirection:
Size every window for its worst-case string, then test it.
- Speed: give the window room for '88 888.8 m/s | HDG 888°', or drop the decimal at 10 km/s and above ('10 848 m/s').
- Clock: put the PHYSICS/RAILS word on the UT line, or abbreviate it, so 'T+ 88d 88:88:88' and '×100 000' both fit.
- Apsis rows: two lines, value right and countdown under it, or shorten the countdown to 'T− 10d 08h'.
- Target rows: let the value wrap under the label.
- Lab: add a 'tli' scene (10.85 km/s, ×4 physics at 2d+, 10-day countdowns) and a 'lunarReturnEntry' scene (11 km/s surface).
- Spec: extend the overflow assertion so every text node's box lies inside its panel's padding box in those scenes.

findings.defect: The next-stage tile cuts its name and its action line with an ellipsis. This tile is the one that tells the player what Space will do next. In the drogue phase it hides the key word: 'release drogues · deploy mai…'. At M-1 separation it drops 'jettison fairing'. From lunar lift-off to entry it reads 'Capsule separ…' for about four game days. The active tile was given a wrap for long names this round, but the next tile, which matters more for a hand-fired stack, was not.
findings.realReference: KSP's stage stack never truncates what the next stage holds: each part in the next stage is shown as an icon and its tooltip names it. The brief says 'a stage stack that the player fires by hand', so the player has to read exactly what fires.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/hud/hudStyles.ts lines 291 and 294: .tile .name and .tile .meta are white-space: nowrap/pre with overflow: hidden and text-overflow: ellipsis. The 'Space' key chip (.hint) takes about a quarter of l1. Only .tile.active .l1 gets flex-wrap (lines 306-307).
findings.fixDirection:
Never ellipsize the next tile.
- Let its name wrap to two lines, and move the Space chip to the icon column or under the name.
- Let the action line wrap, or use shorter words ('sep. motors · tower · fairing'), and never cut a chute's name.
- Add a spec check over every stage of every vehicle def: the next tile's .name and .meta have scrollWidth <= clientWidth at 720p.
- Optionally say what the stage lights, e.g. 'M-3 separation → Heron descent stage'.

findings.defect:
In the real game, the stage list's delta-v does not add up to the total above it while in air, and the upper stages are understated about threefold.
- Pad (app pad-chase): the header reads 'Δv 20 200 m/s total', but the rows read Lunar lift-off 1 001 + M-3 sep 1 028 + M-2 sep 2 302 + M-1 sep 4 211 + Launch 3 267 = 11 809 m/s. The same lift-off stage reads 3 408 m/s in space (mission 05).
- At 4 km (climb-chase-4km): 19 487 against a sum of 14 427.
- At 15 km (mission 02): 18 844 against 17 855.
- At 76.9 km (mission 03) the rows add up exactly (16 552), which shows the rows use the current air pressure and the header uses vacuum.
Nothing labels which basis is used. A player planning the mission on the pad reads a lunar ascent stage worth 1 001 m/s. The lab hides the fault: its pad sums to the total (12 332) because its deltaVNow equals deltaVVac.
findings.realReference: KSP's delta-v readouts name their situation (ASL / vacuum / current altitude, chosen in the Δv app). The total and the per-stage figures always use the same basis, and an upper stage is quoted in vacuum.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/model.ts describeStages (lines 548 and 560): every row is formatDeltaV(info.deltaVNow), at the current pressure, while the header is readouts.deltaVTotal, which is vacuum.
findings.fixDirection:
Show vacuum delta-v for every stage that is not burning (they fire high up), and the current-pressure figure only on the active tile, with its basis shown ('Δv 2 392 m/s now · 2 772 vac').
- Make the header total the sum of the figures shown, or label it 'VAC'.
- Give labs/flight-ui/flightState.ts a pad state with deltaVNow != deltaVVac.
- Add a unit test that the rows sum to the header on the same basis.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\mission\10-lunar-touchdown-chase.png ('ALTITUDE · DATUM · AUTO −1 902 m', landed); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\cockpit\app-lunar-surface-seat.png and app\start-lunar-surface-cockpit.png (after this round: the MFD FLT altitude box '−1902 m'); mission\11-lunar-liftoff-chase.png ('RADAR 54.0 m'); flight-ui\pad-720p.png ('SEA LEVEL 75.0 m') against flight-ui\real-pad-720p.png ('RADAR 18.0 m', same T+ 00:00:00); mission\17-splashdown-chase.png ('−0.1 m'); flight-ui\mfd-pages-hover-720p.png (FLT 4.0 m beside LND RADAR ALT 0.0 m)
findings.defect:
The AUTO altimeter reads the datum or sea-level height whenever the vessel is landed, and radar height otherwise.
- At Tranquility Base the primary altitude reads '−1 902 m' with the vessel standing on its gear. The number looks as if the lander is underground, and it is the one thing a pilot reads at touchdown.
- When the lander lifts off, the readout jumps to '54.0 m RADAR'.
- On the pad it jumps from 75.0 m to 18.0 m at clamp release.
- At splashdown it shows '−0.1 m'.
The lab hides all of this, because its Moon terrain is at the datum (landed reads 4.0 m).
findings.realReference: KSP's automatic altimeter shows terrain (radar) altitude near the ground, landed included, so a landed craft reads a few metres. Apollo's landing displays read altitude above the surface. An altimeter should not jump at the moment of lift-off.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/model.ts altitudeSource (line 52): `!isLanded(activeVesselOf(s)) && altitudeRadar < RADAR_ALTITUDE_SWITCH ? 'radar' : 'asl'`. 'Landed' forces ASL, so a site off the datum shows its datum height. formatAltitude prints −0.1 m when the vessel floats slightly below sea level.
findings.fixDirection:
In AUTO, use the radar height whenever it is below 2 km, landed included, clamped at 0 (or measured from the lowest point), and show LANDED / SPLASHED in the altimeter title. Then touchdown reads about 0-4 m and lift-off continues from it.
- Clamp to 0 m when landed or splashed.
- Add a lab scene landed at a non-datum site (Tranquility at −1.9 km) and a spec check that landed means |altitude| < 5 m on the HUD and on the MFD FLT and LND pages.

findings.defect: The chute light is the readout that was reported as wrong ('RISKY'), and it still lights where chutes cannot work. On the airless Moon the ENT page reads drogue deploy RISKY in orbit and SAFE in green on the surface. A green SAFE for a parachute on the Moon is wrong at a glance. In the same composites, Mach, angle of attack and lift vector correctly read '—'.
findings.realReference: Parachute deploy indicators (KSP's chute safety colours, Orion's and Apollo's ELS) only mean anything in an atmosphere. Without air there is no 'safe' deployment. The brief asks for correct information.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/model.ts describeChuteEnvelope (line 787) passes Readouts.chuteEnvelope straight through. The sim's chuteEnvelope (src/sim/vessel/modules/parachute.ts, inside()) tests altitude, Mach, speed and q against the envelope with no air check, so q = 0 and Mach 0 on the Moon pass as 'safe'. The lab copies that rule.
findings.fixDirection: Apply the rule this round used for Mach: when !inAtmosphere (no atmosphere, or above simTop), describeChuteEnvelope returns a neutral 'NO AIR' / '—' light. File a sim request so chuteEnvelope is null without air. Add a spec check: on the Moon the ENT page's chute row shows '—'.

findings.defect: In the first minute of every launch, the RECOVERY panel's DOWN-RANGE and CROSS-RANGE swing between 'ahead' and 'behind' and between 'left' and 'right', by up to 3 000 km, from one shot to the next. Over the same shots DISTANCE (2 298 km), BEARING (131°) and IMPACT MISS (2 298 km · 314°) do not move. The ground track they resolve against is the heading of 0.1-9 m/s of horizontal drift during a vertical climb (HDG 270°, 272°, 100°, 276° in the same shots).
findings.realReference: Range-safety and recovery displays resolve down-range and cross-range against the planned ground track or launch azimuth, never against noise. In vertical flight they show distance and bearing only, as the HUD already does under chutes ('GROUND TRACK vertical').
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/model.ts describeLandingTarget (around line 177): `const tracked = s.readouts.horizontalSpeed >= 0.1`. A threshold of 0.1 m/s takes drift and the Earth's rotation as a track.
findings.fixDirection: Resolve along the track only above a real horizontal speed (for example 50 m/s, or a flight-path angle below about 75°), with hysteresis. Below that, show 'GROUND TRACK vertical' as the chutes view does, or resolve against the launch azimuth from the LAUNCH panel (099°). Add a unit test: horizontal speed 2 m/s at pitch 89° gives no down-range or cross-range rows.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\mfd-pages-720p.png and mfd-pages-native.png (STG 'STACK · 5 STAGES LEFT · 1 BURNING' with SYS 'THRUST 0.0 kN', throttle 0 %; STG footer 'ΔV REMAINING 3 341 m/s' beside ORB 'ΔV REMAINING 120 m/s'; SYS 'TWR 0.00' beside STG 'ACTIVE TWR 1.98'); mfd-pages-native-reentry.png (SYS 'MASS 6 120 kg' against '28.5 t' in the others); app\start-trans-earth.png and mission stills (warp limiter: 'Limited to ×10 000: Altitude too low…' against 'Limited to ×4: under acceleration…')
findings.defect:
The MFD wording contradicts itself within one composite.
- 'BURNING' is printed while the engine is off.
- Two different quantities are both called 'ΔV REMAINING': 120 m/s is the maneuver node's, 3 341 m/s is the whole vessel's.
- 'TWR 0.00' and 'TWR 1.98' appear side by side.
- The mass unit flips from t to kg between states.
- The warp-limiter reasons mix sentence case and lower case.
findings.realReference: KSP labels its fields 'Δv (stage)', 'Δv (total)' and 'Burn time (node)'. Shipped HUDs keep one unit and one name per quantity.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/mfd/mfdPainter.ts: the STG summary header uses 'BURNING' for the active stage, the footer label is 'ΔV REMAINING' for deltaVTotal, the SYS 'TWR' row is the current thrust over weight, and mass is formatted with an automatic unit. The limiter text is the sim's limitedBy, shown as is (src/ui/model.ts describeWarp).
findings.fixDirection:
- STG header: 'ACTIVE' (or 'BURNING' only while thrust > 0).
- STG footer: 'ΔV TOTAL', matching SYS.
- SYS: 'TWR NOW' (or 'THRUST/WT').
- Mass: always in t, with one decimal below 10 t.
- Lower-case the first letter of limitedBy after the colon.

findings.defect: A vessel standing on the pad reads 0.88 g in one shot and 1.00 g in another taken at the same instant. The G LOAD gauge should read 1.00 g while the vessel is held on the ground.
findings.realReference: The proper acceleration of a vehicle at rest on the ground is 1 g.
findings.likelyCause: The sim's gLoad at scene start, while the vessel is still settling on the clamps (holdOnGround). The HUD shows what the sim reports.
findings.fixDirection: Request the sim owner to report gLoad = |g_local| / g0 while landed or clamped. Optionally, have the HUD show 1.00 g whenever isLanded.
